tools.name: get_vulnerability
tools.description: Get the merged entry for one or more IDs: CVE, GitHub advisory (GHSA), EUVD, or an OSV ID such as PYSEC, GO or RUSTSEC. Returns the description, CVSS, CISA KEV status, EPSS, public exploits, affected packages, fixed versions, priority and source links.

tools.name: get_poc
tools.description: List the public exploit code and proofs of concept the sources link to one vulnerability: Metasploit exploit modules, Exploit-DB entries, references NVD or the CNA tagged as exploits (broken links left out), and GitHub PoC repositories (most stars first). Links only; nothing is downloaded or run. Th

tools.name: get_overview
tools.description: Get the stored AI-written overview of one CVE: one paragraph on what the flaw is, what it affects, what an attacker can do, whether it is exploited and how to fix it, written by Hinoki Offensive One from the entry's source data. Overviews are written only when someone opens the CVE page on vulnerabl

tools.name: search
tools.description: Search the whole catalog by words: product, vendor, package, CVE ID, common vulnerability name, research metadata or description text. Best match first by default. Each result says which fields matched. When nothing matches, the reply suggests a broader query.

tools.name: get_package
tools.description: Every known vulnerability in one open source package, most urgent first, with the affected ranges and fixed versions published for that package. Give a version to learn which advisories affect it and the lowest upgrade that leaves every affecting range.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Look up a vendor product such as an operating system, browser, server or appliance. With only a product name, returns a clear match or lists candidates. Give a version to see affected entries and the lowest upgrade that clears them. For WordPress core, plugins or themes, use get_wordpress.

tools.name: list_feed
tools.description: Follow new or changed catalog entries. Defaults to newest first, or newest CISA KEV additions when kev is true. For incremental sync, pass modified_since with sort=modified. Use search for best matches to a text query.

tools.name: top_priority
tools.description: What to patch first: the vulnerabilities with the highest priority score (exploitation, EPSS, CVSS, automatability) among those with activity in a time window, optionally narrowed to an ecosystem, vendor or product.

tools.name: check_stack
tools.description: Find known vulnerabilities in package versions and website technologies, ranked by what to fix first. Send a version list, lockfile, CycloneDX or SPDX SBOM, or Wappalyzer export. For a WordPress inventory of core, plugins and themes, use check_wordpress.

tools.name: get_wordpress
tools.description: Every known vulnerability in one WordPress plugin or theme, by its wordpress.org slug, or in WordPress core, most urgent first, with affected versions and fixes from Wordfence Intelligence and the CVE records. Without a slug, a name such as "Contact Form 7" is matched: a clear match is answered dire

tools.name: check_wordpress
tools.description: Check every version a WordPress site runs: the core version and its plugins and themes, as {slug, version} lists or the raw output of wp plugin list and wp theme list (table, CSV or JSON). Returns, most urgent first, which installed versions are affected, by which entries, and what to update to. Plu

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_poc, list_feed · Private data: get_poc, get_wordpress, check_wordpress · Public sink: check_stack · Destructive: get_poc.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_poc, list_feed · Private data: get_poc, get_wordpress, check_wordpress · Public sink: check_stack · Destructive: get_poc

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "get_product" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
